title: Only 2^{O(n^2)} triangulated 3-spheres on n vertices?
credit: Gap stated by Kalai (1988), Pfeifle–Ziegler (2004), Nevo–Wilson (2013), Nevo–Santos–Wilson (2016).
premise_risks: Closing this specific log factor is a natural open gap but not singled out as a numbered open problem in the sources; Nevo–Santos–Wilson call their lower bound 'close to' the upper bound.
Durhuus–Pavelka (Nov 2026) is unrefereed; used only for context on the facet version.
plain: Count the triangulations of the 3-dimensional sphere on n labelled vertices. Constructions give at least 2^{cn^2} of them, while the only upper bound, from counting all possible sets of tetrahedra, is 2^{Cn^2 log n}. Decide which is the truth: is the count at most 2^{Cn^2}, or does the log n factor really occur?
math: Let $s(n)$ be the number of simplicial complexes $K$ on vertex set $[n]$ (every vertex used) with $|K|\cong S^3$. Known: $2^{\Omega(n^2)}\le s(n)\le 2^{O(n^2\log n)}$. Decide whether $\log_2 s(n)=O(n^2)$ (i.e. $\exists C\ \forall n:\ s(n)\le 2^{Cn^2}$) or $\log_2 s(n)/n^2\to\infty$ along some subsequence.
